decisions.reason: As an environmental sensor module it remains close to the firm's core modular hardware, firmware and API knowledge, though sensor-specific sourcing, calibration and demand uncertainty make it less secure than the most established core modules.

Because it is a new generation of an existing voltage-measurement function, it builds on strong prior knowledge, proven customer use and well-developed improvement capabilities, so continuation is very likely.

The MQTT proxy fits the firm's software and connectivity capabilities, but as a standalone software-side complement it is easier to absorb into other tools or discontinue if usage and maintenance economics are not compelling.
A CAN bus interface extends the platform into nearby automation and embedded communication applications that the firm can understand, support and improve with its existing technical base.

The touch panel accessory is more peripheral to the firm's main sensing, control and communication platform, so it offers weaker cumulative learning benefits and is the clearest candidate to free resources for core modules and new development.
